research_concepts: PULL_UP as a counter play type
share of units with positive lift (>=70%) and median lift >2pp
methodological_questions: How are 'PNR fail', 'PULL_UP' and 'lift' defined without using the outcome being measured?
What is the unit (team-season, player, defender) and is exposure per unit enough to resolve a 2pp lift?
What baseline defines lift (the same unit's PULL_UP efficiency vs the league, or after-fail vs not-after-fail)?
How to separate regression to the mean, shot-quality and matchup confounding, and a mechanical floor from a real counter effect?
How to handle multiple testing, placebo comparisons and out-of-sample replication?

historical_evidence.finding: Family-level lifts were small and sometimes negative (e.g. POR vs SAS PNR -4.1pp), while player-channel lifts were large on small n (cells of 15-54 possessions). Recorded failure mechanism: A_unanswerable, limited by insufficient exposure (RISK:EXPOSURE_SPARSITY). Only 4 games, no holdout.

On-ball coverage labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup/PBP fields were confident on only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of possessions. switches_on was not populated. Recorded risks: LABEL_ERROR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER. Verdict: failed_gate.
Defense play-type edges vs the league were descriptive. The record notes that edges depend only on the defense (e.g. DAL PNR +9.2% against every offense), so they are not matchup-specific.

Pre-game play-type PPP ranks predicted held-out efficiency (median rho +0.539; 90.8% positive top-3 lift). The recorded failure mechanism is C_artifact: top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types. RISK:DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY is recorded.

Equilibrium and actual-mix matchup predictors had negative holdout R2 (-0.1981 and -0.7167) against a team-mean R2 of +0.1197 (520 cells, 69,876 possessions). Failure mechanism: B_powered_null. Verdict: tool_eval_fail.
The in-game adapter PPP lift did not carry over to Game N+1 (powered null, no PPP lift). The handoff says not to cite the earlier calibrated numbers.
Year-over-year r = -0.023 on 62 pairs. With about 100 possessions per team-season, deltas of +/-0.05 PPP are within sampling noise. Failure mechanism: A_unanswerable.
Shot-quality (xPPP) features added lift of only +0.0054, below the +0.02 real-signal threshold (powered null).
PBP-derived shot-level PNR rates are descriptive and range from about 7.6% to 13.8% of half-court shots by team. They are a calibration input only. The record gives no pass/fail gate.
Raw TOV-force channel lifts shrank by about 50% or more under adversarial re-routing. The net lift is model-implied rather than observed, on 4 games.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball defensive coverage from NBA matchup/PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Low confident-label rates (3.3-14.9%) and an unpopulated switches_on field (LABEL_ERROR, small sample).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-channel and matchup lift decomposition on small cells
failed_approaches.why: Insufficient exposure (cell n 15-54); helper steals contaminate defender attribution; no holdout.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matchup-level equilibrium and actual-mix predictors of PPP
failed_approaches.why: Negative holdout R2 versus simple team means (powered null).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Carryover of an in-game counter-adaptation lift to the next game
failed_approaches.why: Powered null: the lift did not replicate out of sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading broad positive lift as a real effect
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: the lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types rather than the targeted mechanism.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record directly tests PULL_UP as a counter after PNR failure, so the question has not been answered before.
Earlier work records that on-ball coverage and PNR-failure labels from this PBP and matchup data are unreliable (FAM:SF-APPS-058).
Earlier work records that small-n unit or channel lifts are noisy and exposure-limited (FAM:SF-APPA-066, FAM:SF-APPA-029).
Earlier work records that league-wide play-type efficiency can produce apparent lift as an artifact (FAM:SF-APPA-063).
Earlier work records that counter-adaptation lifts have failed to replicate out of sample (FAM:SF-CHT-020).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP efficiency differs after a PNR failure, at any level of aggregation.
Whether a 70%-of-units and 2pp-median criterion is reachable at realistic per-unit exposure.
Whether a PNR-failure definition based only on pre-shot information (not on the outcome) exists in this data.
Anything about the 2025-26 playoffs, which were only partial on the question date.
own_inferences: As posed, 'lift', 'unit' and 'PNR fail' are all undefined. If failure is defined by a bad defensive outcome (e.g. a made shot, a foul, or a drive) and PULL_UP is scored on the same possessions, a positive lift is partly built in (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, MECHANICAL_FLOOR).

The 'share of units with lift>0' criterion is weak. With pure noise and no true effect, about half of units are positive. 70% is a meaningful bar only when units are large enough to make the sign reliable.

With typical team-season PULL_UP counts after PNR failure of perhaps tens to low hundreds, the standard error of a PPP difference is about 0.08-0.15, much larger than 2pp. Sign noise alone would then keep the share below 70%, so a rejection could simply reflect low power.
PULL_UP may be selected when the defense is already conceding space. That makes the baseline comparison confounded by defender, drop depth and shooter skill.
A median test over many team-seasons is more plausible than a share test, if the pooled sample is large enough.
uncertainties: How many PNR-failure possessions can be identified from PBP and derived play-type records.
Whether the derived graph-database play-type labels include PULL_UP and its relation to PNR (e.g. as a sub-type or a later action).
Whether the 2pp threshold is in PPP, eFG or shot-probability terms.
Whether 'units' means teams, players or team-seasons.
How stable the labelling is across the four seasons of data.

historical_effect.explanation: The records changed the decision from a plain 'proceed' to 'proceed_with_changes'. They show label unreliability (APPS-058), exposure sparsity (APPA-066, APPA-029), artifacts from league-wide effects (APPA-063) and non-replicating lifts (CHT-020). I therefore require a pre-shot PNR-failure definition, exposure gates, league-baseline and placebo controls, and a holdout replication. None of these records tested the question itself, so the decision rests partly on my own inference.

research_concepts: pull-up jump shot as counter to defensive coverage
unit-level lift consistency (share of units with positive lift)
methodological_questions: How should lift in pull-up efficiency be defined and baselined (percentage points vs. expected)?
What counts as a unit (team, player, team-season, lineup) and is there enough exposure per unit?
How to define PNR defensive failure without using outcome-derived labels?
How to guard against regression to the mean, selection, and confounding by shot quality and defender/matchup?
How to set thresholds (>=70% of units positive, median lift >2pp) and handle multiple testing and a placebo/null comparison?
args.query: PNR failure then PULL_UP counter lift league-wide share of units positive median lift 2pp

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

- testability.p_testable: probability that the question can be answered with the stated data at useful statistical power.
